headlineClaims.title: PR picker fills idle and briefly busy owned minis before Blacksmith
headlineClaims.metric: share of PR CI attempt-1 macOS 26 job-minutes on owned minis
headlineClaims.measurementWindow: runs created 2026-09-26 00:45 to 02:17Z (before, 144 runs) against 02:17 to 04:00Z (after, 60 runs)
headlineClaims.population: attempt 1 of in-repository pull_request CI runs, macOS 26 jobs that ran; macOS 15 jobs (no owned pool) excluded
headlineClaims.note: 56.2% to 88.9% owned; Blacksmith macOS 26 job-minutes per run 6.5 to 1.3, and runs touching Blacksmith 38% to 3%. Caveats: (1) The before baseline is not stable: by half-hour of first job it read 45%, 39%, 85% and 59% owned, and the 01:30 slot reached 85% under the old picker with 42 runs. (2) Not load-matched: about 94 PR runs an hour before and about 35 after, and the owned fleet had more spare room after (about 14.5 idle runners of 37.9 online before, 18.0 of 39.2 after), which helps placement under either rule. (3) Attempt 1 only. Attempt-3 re-runs of PR CI (Blacksmith by rule) took 260 Blacksmith macOS minutes inside the before window and 540 inside the after window (wall-clock clipped, any run, not only these runs), and ci-dash showed Blacksmith running jobs doubling (6.4 to 13.0 on average). More owned placement can raise mini refusals and so attempt-3 re-runs; how much of that rise this change caused is not measured, and cmux#14766, which stops the rescue cancelling siblings, went live only at 04:02Z. So no fleet-wide Blacksmith saving is claimed. (4) The controller dropped about 2,860 deliveries between 09-25 21:30 and 09-26 03:40Z (hq#734); jobs whose completion never arrived are missing from both sides. The PR body's replay (111 to 35 Blacksmith jobs) is modeled and not claimed. A daytime, load-matched comparison is still open.

headlineClaims.title: UI E2E runs adopt the app and UI test bundle PR CI compiled
headlineClaims.metric: UI E2E run creation to test start, one selector, product already published at dispatch
headlineClaims.population: One full-build UI E2E run on an owned mini (glaeda-root-std-xcode-26.6) against one adopted-product run on blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-26
headlineClaims.note: 659 s to 250 s from run creation to test start; the build-job window alone went 566 s to 109 s (457 s), but time before the build job grew from 93 s to 141 s (a 119 s Blacksmith queue), so the run-level figure is claimed. This is the best case: the adopted run found a finished product. When the dispatch starts while admission is still compiling, the dispatcher now waits for it (up to 50 min), and the saving is the compile step minus that remaining wait, which can be negative: #14746's own head (this before run, created 22:32:38) had an admission that published at about 22:41, so waiting for it and then adopting (93 to 141 s before the build job plus about 109 s to tests) would have started its tests at about 22:44 to 22:45, roughly 0.5 to 1.5 min later than the 22:43:37 they did. Run creation to test start never includes the dispatcher's wait, because the dispatcher waits before it creates the run. One run each side, on different pools: the old run compiled on an owned mini, the new one adopted a Blacksmith-compiled product on Blacksmith, because products never cross toolchain families. The removed work is the 448 s compile step, so the pool difference matters less than it would for a compile comparison, but it is not like-for-like. Whole run (created to last update, not the PR table's 976 s job-span figure) went from 982 s to 341 s; about 193 s of the old figure is a late product upload after the tests that the adopted run skips, so the whole-run delta is not claimed separately. Only UI runs whose commit has an in-repository PR CI product on macOS 26 benefit. The PR merged at 04:33:43Z and had no adopted production runs yet at recording time, so this stays observed until a median over post-merge UI runs exists.

headlineClaims.population: Pull-request macOS overflow work in the sampled CMUX CI day
headlineClaims.note: This moves workload onto sponsored capacity; it does not claim the compute disappeared.

headlineClaims.title: Trigger the persistent Mac router once per CI run
headlineClaims.metric: router-runs-avoided-per-day
headlineClaims.population: persistent-macos-router workflow invocations
headlineClaims.note: The measured baseline was about 6,864 router runs/day; the once-per-CI-run trigger was expected to produce about 1,253/day, an 82% reduction.

headlineClaims.title: Seed compilation cache on the runner pull requests restore from
headlineClaims.metric: cold-compile-minutes-per-affected-pr
headlineClaims.population: Pull-request admission before the cache producer and consumer runner layouts matched
headlineClaims.note: The PR explicitly left warm compile time unmeasured until the next scheduled seed.

headlineClaims.title: Move Computer Use runtime out of the 3,700-file app module
headlineClaims.metric: warm-incremental-build-time-reduction
headlineClaims.population: comment-only edit to AgentPIDProcessIdentity.swift before and after moving it from the app target to CmuxFoundation
headlineClaims.note: The measured build fell from 38.9 seconds to 13.3 seconds and compiled zero app-target Swift files after the move.

headlineClaims.title: Reuse one warm DerivedData across development tags
headlineClaims.metric: same-commit-tag-build-time-reduction
headlineClaims.population: new development tag at the same commit after a warm build
headlineClaims.note: Fresh DerivedData took 953 seconds; a new tag using the already-warm shared DerivedData took 35.7 seconds.

headlineClaims.title: Stop pull requests from evicting shared cache seeds
headlineClaims.metric: github-cache-occupancy-observed
headlineClaims.population: 27 GitHub cache entries visible to the repository
headlineClaims.note: The oldest macOS entry was only five minutes old and the shared Debug compilation seed was already missing. Pull-request jobs had 14 save+restore cache steps and wrote 1–3 GB PR-scoped entries.

headlineClaims.title: Seed the Debug compilation cache from main
headlineClaims.metric: cold-compile-seconds-per-admission-run
headlineClaims.population: macOS compile admission from an empty compilation cache
headlineClaims.note: The PR deliberately did not quote an unmeasured CI savings number before the scheduled seed had run.

headlineClaims.title: Parallelize slow and history-dependent CI guards
headlineClaims.metric: linux-guard-critical-path-reduction
headlineClaims.population: Linux guard path gating macOS admission
headlineClaims.note: Measured guard wall time fell from 385.5 seconds to 124.3 seconds, about a 68% reduction.

accountingRule: Only claims explicitly marked additive are summed. Baselines, capacity shifts, overlapping savings, and projections stay separate.
